A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeepWeightFlow and contain readable main text, equations, two figures, twenty tables, and Appendices A–K. Content can be reliably matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original weight-generation, transfer-learning, diversity, ablation, and computational-timing results.

after.justification: The same original empirical results remain in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The flow-matching model, Git Re-Basin/TransFusion canonicalization, batch-normalization recalibration, PCA procedures, and conditional variants in Appendix K are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain Iris, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, SVHN, and Yelp coverage, with the same classification, regression, transfer-learning, and conditional-generation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding comparisons, including WeightFlow, FLoWN, RPG, SANE, D2NWG, NM, P-diff, and random/pretrained controls.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, generated-sample counts, metrics, PCA settings, calibration instructions, and transfer-learning protocols remain unchanged, including Tables 12–14 and Appendix J.

E4.justification: Both retain the same canonicalization/capacity, initialization, recalibration, PCA, source-distribution, and diversity analyses. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Seed information and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting are unchanged. Neither version adds a different repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries and findings throughout Tables 1–20 and Figure 2 are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains 93.55 ± 0.13 for canonicalized DeepWeightFlow, and Table 20 retains the same cross-architecture results.

T1.justification: The flow-matching and permutation mathematics, recalibration equations, dual-PCA derivation, and complexity analysis are unchanged. Repositioned equations and Algorithm 1 retain their content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about complete weight generation, scalability, efficiency, diversity, transfer learning, and canonicalization.

C2.justification: Both retain the same capacity-dependent interpretation of canonicalization, scalability qualifications, and explanation of poor joint dataset/architecture generation in Appendix K.2.

D1.justification: The acknowledgements newly identify Voltage Park as a computational-resource provider. This is limited resource-provenance disclosure; hardware specifications, implementation settings, code access, and data-availability statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Research positioning and the distinct cited works are unchanged. The two duplicate MetaDiff entries labeled Zhang et al. 2024a/2024b are consolidated into one 2024 reference, constituting bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: v2 revises the byline and affiliations, adds Author Contributions and an Appendix heading, expands acknowledgements, and consolidates the duplicate reference. The visible byline omits Robin Walters and changes Moritz Laber to Maritz Laber; scientific prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 compacts the author block, reduces Figures 1–2, tightens table spacing, and repositions floats. Table 20 moves from page 25 to page 24. Figure content, captions, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Scientific content is unchanged. Contribution and funding disclosures and bibliography cleanup provide modest benefits, but v2 introduces inconsistent author identification: Robin Walters is absent from the byline despite his retained email, metadata, and contribution initials, while Maritz conflicts with Moritz in the metadata. These attribution defects outweigh the limited editorial improvements.
